A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Topological Schrödinger Bridge Matching. All 42 pages, including Appendices A–F, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F report original Gaussian-bridge simulations, signal-generation and matching experiments, ablations, and computational measurements.

after.justification: The same original empirical studies remain, with results in Table 1, Tables F.1–F.8 and the experimental figures.

M1.justification: The topology-dependent reference dynamics, Gaussian bridge construction, policy networks and likelihood-training objectives are retained. The appendix corrections do not establish an altered algorithm.

E1.justification: Both retain the synthetic graph and edge-GP tests, heat-flow, seismic, traffic, ocean-current, brain-signal and single-cell applications, and Swiss-roll computational scaling scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including SB-BM/VE/VP and the GSB-BM/VE comparisons where reported.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F retain the same preprocessing, split rules, model configurations, training settings, evaluation metrics and computational measurement procedures.

E4.justification: The policy-network comparisons, Gaussian-prior analysis, graph-normalization ablation, intermediate single-cell predictions and computational scaling analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains its five-run reporting, and the same uncertainty entries appear throughout the experimental tables. No run-count, seed or statistical-reporting changes are introduced.

E6.justification: All experimental tables, figures and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same seismic W1 value of 7.69 ± 0.04 for TSB-VE in both versions.

T1.justification: Theorem A.6 qualifies uniqueness as 'up to scaling' and replaces sigma-finite measures with functions. Proposition C.1 revises the endpoint-measure expression and time-marginal factorization; Appendix D.5 replaces C_sigma* with the defined covariance C. These are localized formal revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: the topological SB formulation, closed-form Gaussian bridges, likelihood-trained models and empirical benefits of incorporating topology.

C2.justification: The interpretations of topology's benefits, qualifications concerning ocean-current matching, fixed-topology limitation and future directions in Section 7 and Appendix F remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information, data-processing instructions and code/data access links are unchanged, including the reproducibility statement and Appendix F.

R1.justification: Proposition C.1 adds attribution to Jamison (1975), already cited elsewhere and present in the bibliography. This is a limited citation addition without broader changes in research positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized wording and notation edits, added pointers to Lemma B.6, a paragraph break in Appendix B.3 and time-index renaming in Equation B.14. The section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Revised appendix passages cause small changes in equation wrapping and paragraph spacing, particularly on pages 19, 21 and 25. All figures and tables retain their presentation and placement.

improvement.justification: The uniqueness qualification in Theorem A.6 and covariance correction in D.5 improve precision. However, C.1 replaces an explicit endpoint-density factorization with an integral over the entire endpoint space equated to P01, creating ambiguity between a measure and its total mass. These competing local effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment; the method and empirical evidence are unchanged.
